title: Congressman Brandon Gill addresses Columbus Day and raises concerns about public figures
text:
← Back to the wire
Congressman Brandon Gill addresses Columbus Day and raises concerns about public figures
Congressman Brandon Gill posted on Twitter between October 12 and October 14, 2026, marking Columbus Day and raising questions about Abdul El-Sayed’s alleged family ties and Ilhan Omar’s eligibility regarding immigration issues.
Congressman Brandon Gill, who won the 2024 general election against Ernest Lineberger III with 62.1% of the vote, recently shared a series of posts on his official Twitter account addressing national holidays and concerns about public figures' backgrounds.
On October 12, 2026, Gill marked a federal holiday by posting "Happy Columbus Day!"
The following day, October 13, he commented on allegations involving Abdul El-Sayed and his family’s reported connections to an Islamist organization. In his post, Gill stated, "Abdul El-Sayed’s own sister posted that their family has long been tied to the Muslim Brotherhood. He told Americans there were no ties, then called the question Islamophobic. People are sick of being slandered for asking straightforward questions."
On October 14, Gill questioned the integrity of another member of Congress in relation to immigration policy. He wrote, "American citizenship is the most valuable thing in the world. If Ilhan Omar committed immigration fraud to get it, how can she be trusted to stop immigration fraud as a member of Congress?"
Brandon Gill's remarks reflect ongoing debates over public officials’ backgrounds and U.S. immigration policy. His victory in 2024 secured him a seat in Congress after defeating Ernest Lineberger III by a significant margin.
